definitions.explanation: The deepest underlying layer or foundation of something abstract, such as a belief system, culture, or way of thinking. Emphasizes what lies at the very bottom, supporting everything above it.

examples.japanese: {信頼|しんらい}が{関係|かんけい}の{根底|こんてい}にある。
examples.english: Trust lies at the foundation of the relationship.

examples.japanese: その{考|かんが}えは{社会|しゃかい}の{根底|こんてい}を{揺|ゆ}るがす。
examples.english: That idea shakes the very foundations of society.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{行動|こうどう}の{根底|こんてい}には、{家族|かぞく}への{深|ふか}い{愛情|あいじょう}がある。
examples.english: Deep love for his family lies at the root of his actions.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {根底|こんてい}にある: to lie at the foundation of
- {根底|こんてい}から{覆|くつがえ}す: to overturn from the foundations
- {根底|こんてい}を{揺|ゆ}るがす: to shake the very foundations
- {根底|こんてい}から{崩|くず}れる: to collapse from the base

USAGE:
{根底|こんてい} is almost always used for abstract things — beliefs, relationships, systems, cultures. The most characteristic pattern is {根底|こんてい}にある (to underlie), describing what exists at the deepest level.

SIMILAR WORDS:
{根本|こんぽん} focuses on the fundamental origin or cause. {根底|こんてい} emphasizes the deepest underlying layer that supports everything above it.
